correctness.rationale: Each integer map T_b:x→{bx} preserves Lebesgue measure and compositions multiply slopes. For B≥1 exact branch overlap ∫H_q(x)H_q({Bx})dx equals 0 when B≡0 mod q and otherwise (q−r)/(q²B), r=B mod q, including n=0 via B=1. The q-state weighted residue update L_{r,s}=Σ_{b:br≡s mod q}π_b/b yields C_q(n)=q^−2 e1 L^n d and convergent rational generating function. All terms are nonnegative and strict positivity of all words proves covariance vanishes iff every length-n slope product is divisible by q. Minimum prime valuations m_ell characterize first such n as max_ell ceil(v_ell(q)/m_ell); a zero minimum yields positivity forever. For two slopes 2,3 and q=6, every mixed word contributes zero, while all-two and all-three words give exact parity α_n and formula [α_n(p/2)^n+3((1−p)/3)^n]/36. Positive bounded periodic coefficients give nth-root ρ=max(p/2,(1−p)/3), uniquely minimized at p=2/5 with ρ=1/5. This is one centered interval covariance observable, not finite memory or decorrelation of all observables.

value.rationale: Centered rational subinterval indicators are natural coarse-grained observations of stationary expanding maps. Exactly when their correlations vanish after a finite lag is an intrinsic arithmetic question, not a cosmetic reformulation of qualitative mixing. The complete prime-valuation cutoff and explicit q=6 competition between two deterministic slopes give a sharp and surprising interior switching optimum 2/5 with exponential rate 1/5; it is useful precisely for this observable, without claiming a universal optimal mixing theorem.
